![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14224501/assets/66ab1a3e2e7244a9b3e5fc9bda814736194c28dd9438fbb97086e99be4633261.png)

Evaluate ${∮}_{C}(\sqrt{x}-4{x}^{2}y)dx+({e}^{y}+4x{y}^{2})\,dy,$ where the path $C$ is shown above.
question.worked_solution:
Green's theorem states that

$$
{∮}_{C}P\,dx+Q\,dy={∬}_{D}(\frac{∂Q}{∂x}-\frac{∂P}{∂y})\,\text{d}A.
$$

In our case, the region $D$ and its boundary $C$ satisfy the conditions of Green's theorem:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14224501/assets/709d108b2b992d1714c7c0b3bef26f52e965c2467f38d05103cd45f4f9bc821b.png)

Now, since 

$$
P(x,y)=\sqrt{x}-4{x}^{2}y,\,Q(x,y)={e}^{y}+4x{y}^{2},
$$

 

we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂P}{∂y}=-4{x}^{2},\,\frac{∂Q}{∂x}=4{y}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Applying Green's theorem, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{∮}_{C}(\sqrt{x}-4{x}^{2}y)dx+({e}^{y}+4x{y}^{2})\,dy & ={∬}_{D}(\frac{∂Q}{∂x}-\frac{∂P}{∂y})\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(4{y}^{2}-(-4{x}^{2}))\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}4({x}^{2}+{y}^{2})\,\text{d}A\end{aligned}
$$

Now, notice that the region $D$ can be represented in polar coordinates as

$$
Δ=\{(r,\theta )\,:\,0\le r\le 2,\,0\le \theta \le \frac{\pi }{2}\}.
$$

The change of variables formula for plane polar coordinates states that

$$
{∬}_{D}f(x,y)\text{ }dA={∬}_{Δ}\text{ }f(r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta )\,r\text{ }drd\theta .
$$

Finally, we can calculate our double integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}4({x}^{2}+{y}^{2})\,\text{d}A & ={∬}_{Δ}4({r}^{2}{cos}^{2}⁡\theta +{r}^{2}{sin}^{2}⁡\theta )\,r\,\text{d}r\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}{\int }_{0}^{2}4{r}^{3}({cos}^{2}⁡\theta +{sin}^{2}⁡\theta )\,\text{d}r\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}{\int }_{0}^{2}4{r}^{3}\,\text{d}r\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}[{r}^{4}]_{0}^{2}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}16\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =16[\theta ]_{0}^{\pi /2} \\  & =16\cdot \frac{\pi }{2} \\  & =8\pi \end{aligned}
$$
